post.caption:
Before factories, most work went by daylight and by task. Machines do not care about daylight and cost money whenever they are idle, so work became hours instead of tasks, and everyone had to agree what time it was. Railways then forced standardised time zones on whole countries, because a timetable needs a single clock. Before that every town kept its own noon. The weekend and the eight-hour day are not traditions either. They were won in response.
